# 12-Week Vegan Muscle-Building Programme

## Client Profile & Goals
Your 26-year-old client is a recreational lifter seeking muscle hypertrophy on a strict vegan diet. With full gym access and a target of 150g daily plant protein, this programme balances progressive overload with adequate recovery and nutritional support for muscle growth.

---

- **Protein**: 150g daily (1.6–1.8g per kg bodyweight, assuming ~85kg)

- **Fats**: 0.8–1.2g per kg bodyweight (hormone production, satiety)

### Vegan Protein Sources (150g daily strategy)
- **Legumes**: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans (15–18g protein per cooked cup)
- **Tofu/Tempeh**: 15–20g protein per 100g serving
- **Seitan**: 25g protein per 100g (highest plant-based option)
- **Nuts & Seeds**: Peanut butter, hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds (8–10g per serving)
- **Whole Grains**: Quinoa, oats, brown rice (8–12g per cooked cup)
- **Vegan Protein Powder**: 20–30g per serving (pea, hemp, or blended)

### Sample Daily Meal Structure
- **Breakfast**: Oatmeal (50g) + peanut butter (2 tbsp) + banana + hemp seeds = ~25g protein
- **Snack 1**: Vegan protein shake (30g powder) + berries = ~30g protein

- **Evening**: Fortified plant milk + vegan protein powder = ~25g protein

## Recovery & Lifestyle

### Sleep
- Target 7–9 hours nightly
- Consistent sleep/wake times
- Cool, dark bedroom
- Extra 30 min sleep on heavy training days if possible

### Stress Management
- 5–10 minute post-workout foam rolling
- 10–15 minute daily stretching or yoga
- Meditation or breathing work (5 min daily)
- Active recovery walks on rest days (optional, 15–20 min)

### Activity
- 1 complete rest day per week (no training)
- Light walking on rest days (optional, 20–30 min)
- Avoid excessive non-training activity (NEAT) on high-volume weeks

### Hydration
- 3–4 litres daily minimum
- Add 500ml on cardio days
- Add electrolytes if sweating heavily (especially on longer cardio sessions)

### Nutrition Timing Around Cardio
- **Pre-Cardio** (30–45 min before): Light carbs + small protein (banana + 10g peanut butter, or rice cakes)
- **Post-Cardio** (within 30 min): Protein + carbs (protein shake + fruit, or tofu + rice)
- **Cardio on Resistance Days**: Perform cardio after resistance or on separate days; ensure adequate carbs

## Tracking & Progression

### Weekly Check-ins
- Log all weights, reps, and RPE on resistance sessions
- Log cardio duration, modality, and perceived intensity
- Assess energy levels and recovery
- Adjust calories if weight stalls >2 weeks

### Cardio Progression
- **Weeks 1–4**: Build base (30–35 min, Zone 2)
- **Weeks 5–8**: Increase duration (35–40 min, Zone 2–3)
- **Weeks 9–12**: Maintain fitness, reduce volume during peaking (25–35 min, Zone 2–3)

### Expected Progress
- **Strength**: 5–10% increase on main lifts over 12 weeks
- **Muscle**: 1–2kg lean mass gain (realistic for vegan diet with proper nutrition)
- **Cardiovascular**: Improved work capacity, lower resting HR, better recovery between sets
- **Body Composition**: Slight fat gain acceptable if protein/training dialled in; cardio helps minimize fat gain

### Adjustments
- If strength stalls: Add 200 kcal, increase protein to 160g, reduce cardio by 1 session
- If fatigue increases: Reduce resistance volume by 20%, reduce cardio to 1–2 sessions, add extra rest day
- If weight loss occurs: Increase calories by 300 kcal, reduce cardio duration by 5–10 min
- If cardio feels too taxing: Reduce intensity to Zone 2 only, or drop to 2 sessions per week

# Complete 12-Week Vegan Muscle-Building Programme (Full Version)

## Client Profile & Goals
Your 26-year-old client is a recreational lifter seeking muscle hypertrophy on a strict vegan diet. With full gym access and a target of 150g daily plant protein, this comprehensive programme balances progressive overload with adequate recovery, nutritional support for muscle growth, strategic cardio, high-protein breakfasts, and a weekly cheat meal. Phase 3 emphasizes maximum intensity and strength development.

## Nutritional Framework

### Daily Targets
- **Calories**: Maintenance + 300–500 kcal surplus (adjust based on progress)
- **Protein**: 150g daily (1.6–1.8g per kg bodyweight, assuming ~85kg)
- **Carbohydrates**: 4–5g per kg bodyweight (supports training and recovery)
- **Fats**: 0.8–1.2g per kg bodyweight (hormone production, satiety)

### Vegan Protein Sources (150g daily strategy)
- **Legumes**: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans (15–18g protein per cooked cup)
- **Tofu/Tempeh**: 15–20g protein per 100g serving
- **Seitan**: 25g protein per 100g (highest plant-based option)
- **Nuts & Seeds**: Peanut butter, hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds (8–10g per serving)
- **Whole Grains**: Quinoa, oats, brown rice (8–12g per cooked cup)
- **Vegan Protein Powder**: 20–30g per serving (pea, hemp, or blended)

# Complete 12-Week Vegan Muscle-Building Programme (Full Version)

## Client Profile & Goals
Your 26-year-old client is a recreational lifter seeking muscle hypertrophy on a strict vegan diet. With full gym access and a target of 150g daily plant protein, this comprehensive programme balances progressive overload with adequate recovery, nutritional support for muscle growth, strategic cardio, high-protein breakfasts, and a weekly cheat meal. Phase 3 emphasizes maximum intensity and strength development.

---

## Nutritional Framework

### Daily Targets
- **Calories**: Maintenance + 300–500 kcal surplus (adjust based on progress)
- **Protein**: 150g daily (1.6–1.8g per kg bodyweight, assuming ~85kg)
- **Carbohydrates**: 4–5g per kg bodyweight (supports training and recovery)
- **Fats**: 0.8–1.2g per kg bodyweight (hormone production, satiety)

### Vegan Protein Sources (150g daily strategy)
- **Legumes**: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans (15–18g protein per cooked cup)
- **Tofu/Tempeh**: 15–20g protein per 100g serving
- **Seitan**: 25g protein per 100g (highest plant-based option)
- **Nuts & Seeds**: Peanut butter, hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds (8–10g per serving)
- **Whole Grains**: Quinoa, oats, brown rice (8–12g per cooked cup)
- **Vegan Protein Powder**: 20–30g per serving (pea, hemp, or blended)

### Sample Daily Meal Structure
- **Breakfast**: Oatmeal (50g) + peanut butter (2 tbsp) + banana + hemp seeds = ~25g protein
- **Snack 1**: Vegan protein shake (30g powder) + berries = ~30g protein
- **Lunch**: Tofu stir-fry (150g) + brown rice (1 cup) + vegetables = ~30g protein
- **Snack 2**: Hummus (¼ cup) + whole grain crackers + almonds = ~15g protein
- **Dinner**: Lentil curry (1.5 cups) + quinoa (¾ cup) + coconut milk = ~25g protein
- **Evening**: Fortified plant milk + vegan protein powder = ~25g protein

**Total: ~150g protein, balanced macros**

### Supplementation Recommendations
- **Vitamin B12**: 2000 IU daily or 2000 mcg weekly (critical for vegans)
- **Vitamin D3**: 2000–4000 IU daily (vegan D3 from lichen)
- **Creatine Monohydrate**: 5g daily (vegan-friendly, supports muscle gains and strength)
- **Omega-3 (ALA/EPA/DHA)**: Algae-based supplement or 1–2 tbsp ground flaxseed daily
- **Iron**: Monitor levels; consider supplementation if deficient (pair with vitamin C)
- **Zinc**: 8–11mg daily (legumes + seeds, or supplement)

### Caloric Adjustment for Cardio
With added cardio, increase daily calories by 150–250 kcal to maintain the surplus and support recovery. Monitor weight weekly; adjust if needed.
